problem_statement: High computational cost and lack of calibrated uncertainty estimates hinder practical deployment of quality estimation in large-scale MT pipelines.

problem_statement: How to improve efficiency and quality of machine translation corpus generation by synergizing human post-editing with large language models.
core_contributions: Introduces LLM-Driven Pseudo Labeling and Translation Recommendation System to reduce annotator workload
Proposes Enhanced Translation Synthesis and Assisted Annotation Analysis using LLMs for improved hypotheses and quality assessment
Extends prior human-in-the-loop MT post-editing framework with real-time, online-trained quality estimation enriched by LLM ensembling
limitations_or_scope: Focuses on semi-automated post-editing for MT corpus expansion; evaluation metrics emphasize quality score improvement and character-level alignment—not full human evaluation or multilingual robustness testing.

problem_statement: Efficient multilingual machine translation without knowledge distillation or autoregressive decoding latency.
core_contributions: Introduces M-DAT: a multilingual non-autoregressive Transformer that eliminates the need for knowledge distillation.
Proposes pivot back-translation (PivotBT) to improve zero-shot generalization in multilingual translation.
Achieves state-of-the-art BLEU scores on supervised and zero-shot translation directions across five benchmarks.
limitations_or_scope: Does not address autoregressive trade-offs like fluency vs. latency; limited discussion of cross-lingual transfer bottlenecks beyond zero-shot directions.

evidence_spans.claim_value: M-DAT eliminates knowledge distillation
evidence_spans.evidence_text: Our system leverages the recent advance of the directed acyclic Transformer (DAT), which does not require KD.

evidence_spans.evidence_text: We further propose a pivot back-translation (PivotBT) approach to improve the generalization to unseen translation directions.

evidence_spans.claim_value: State-of-the-art performance in non-autoregressive MNMT
evidence_spans.evidence_text: Experiments show that our M-DAT achieves state-of-the-art performance in non-autoregressive MNMT.

evidence_spans.claim_value: Evaluated on five datasets including zero-shot test sets
evidence_spans.evidence_text: We evaluated M-DAT on five datasets: WMT-EFD, WMT-EFZ, WMT-MANY, IWSLT, and Europarl.

problem_statement: How to reduce computational cost of large MT models without sacrificing translation quality?
core_contributions: Proposes quality-estimation (QE)-based deferral as a simple, effective rule for cascading MT systems
Demonstrates that cascaded systems using QE deferral match large-model performance while invoking the large model only 30–50% of the time
Validates gains via both automatic metrics and human evaluation across multiple QE models and setups
limitations_or_scope: Effectiveness depends on QE model quality; assumes availability of reliable off-the-shelf QE metrics.

evidence_spans.claim_value: QE-based deferral allows a cascaded system to match the performance of a larger model while invoking it for a small fraction (30% to 50%) of the examples

evidence_spans.claim_value: Validated through both automatic and human evaluation
evidence_spans.evidence_text: We validate this approach through both automatic and human evaluation.

evidence_spans.claim_value: Uses existing quality estimation (QE) metrics as deferral rules
evidence_spans.evidence_text: we propose a simple yet effective approach for machine translation, using existing quality estimation (QE) metrics as deferral rules.

problem_statement: Traditional recommender systems follow a user-platform paradigm that prioritizes platform objectives and aggregate user data, leading to lack of user control, algorithmic manipulation, echo chambers, and bias against less-active users.
core_contributions: Proposes a novel user-agent-platform paradigm to shift control from platform to user via LLM-based agents.
Introduces InstructAgent and Instruct2Agent—instruction-aware, tool-using LLM agents with dynamic memory for individualized recommendation.
Releases InstructRec, a new benchmark of four instruction-augmented recommendation datasets with user intent annotations.
limitations_or_scope: Focused on instruction-driven, LLM-based agents for recommendation; evaluation limited to four curated InstructRec datasets; no real-world deployment or long-term user study reported.

problem_statement: LLMs lack robust multi-step deductive reasoning and real-time factual grounding for expert-level deep research tasks.
core_contributions: Introduces Agentic Reasoning — a framework that augments LLM reasoning with external tool-using agents (web search, code execution, structured memory).
Proposes the Mind Map agent to construct and maintain a structured knowledge graph for tracking logical relationships during deduction.
Demonstrates significant performance gains over RAG systems and closed-source LLMs on PhD-level scientific QA (GPQA) and domain-specific deep research tasks.
limitations_or_scope: Work in progress; evaluation focused on scientific QA and deep research—no multimodal or real-time adaptability yet (future work noted in Discussion).

problem_statement: Most prior instruction tuning methods treat programming languages in isolation, hindering cross-lingual knowledge transfer in code LLMs.
core_contributions: Proposes a multi-agent collaboration framework where language-specific agents jointly generate high-quality multilingual instruction data via memory-augmented discussion.
Introduces x-Instruct — a novel multilingual synthetic instruction dataset (~95K samples across Python, Java, C++, C#, TypeScript, PHP, Bash) built from code snippets.
Trains Qwen2.5-xCoder (32B), a multilingual code LLM that significantly reduces cross-lingual performance gaps on EvalPlus and MultiPL-E benchmarks.
limitations_or_scope: Limited to instruction tuning (SFT + DPO); evaluation focuses on Pass@1; no ablation on agent memory summarization granularity.

evidence_spans.evidence_text: Experimental results on multilingual programming benchmarks demonstrate the superior performance of Qwen2.5-xCoder in sharing common knowledge, highlighting its potential to reduce the cross-lingual gap.

problem_statement: Treating Language Model Agents as 'normal agents' leads to misplaced trust and utility loss due to their inherent ontological instabilities—despite surface-level agentic behavior.
core_contributions: Identifies four intrinsic pathologies of Language Model Agents (LMAs): ontological statelessness, stochasticity, semantic sensitivity, and linguistic intermediation
Argues that LMA scaffolding (e.g., memory, tools, planning) cannot resolve fundamental ontological deficits in agentic identity
Proposes 'agentic evaluations'—empirically grounded measurements of LMA identity properties (identifiability, continuity, persistence, consistency) before, during, and after deployment
limitations_or_scope: Focuses on conceptual and ontological critique—not empirical evaluation or technical implementation; does not propose new benchmarks or datasets.

problem_statement: Current LLM integration in foreign language education lacks grounding in educational methodology, resulting in inflexible, non-adaptive applications that fail to support personalized, inclusive, and pedagogically sound learning.
core_contributions: Proposes a three-role framework for LLMs as tutors in FLE: data enhancers (e.g., material generation, student simulation), task predictors (e.g., assessment, feedback, error correction), and agents (e.g., pedagogically aligned ITS)
Identifies key gaps in current LLM use for FLE—including lack of cultural adaptation, multimodal support, and longitudinal student modeling—and advocates for interdisciplinary research

Introduces conceptual distinctions among discriminative, generative, and mixed task predictors, and outlines foundational agent capabilities (planning, memory, tool use, pedagogical alignment) for LLM-powered tutoring

Proposes SeCom: a segment-level memory construction method using a novel conversation segmentation model

Proposes autonomous note construction with structured attributes (context, keywords, tags) and adaptive link generation between memories.
Enables memory evolution—new memories trigger updates to contextual representations and attributes of existing memories.

problem_statement: RAG systems suffer from retrieval inefficiency and LLMs’ inability to filter irrelevant information, leading to hallucinations and degraded performance under long inputs.
core_contributions: Introduces ParetoRAG: an unsupervised, sentence-level RAG refinement framework guided by the Pareto principle.
Achieves dual improvements in retrieval precision and generation quality without additional training or API calls.
Reduces token consumption by 70% while improving answer accuracy and fluency across diverse datasets, LLMs, and retrievers.
limitations_or_scope: Limited to sentence-level decomposition and weighting; assumes paragraph-to-sentence structure; no ablation on extreme noise or domain shift beyond reported robustness analysis.

evidence_spans.claim_value: requires neither additional training resources nor extra API calls

problem_statement: Small-scale LLMs suffer from knowledge staleness and are highly sensitive to noisy or irrelevant retrieved content in RAG, leading to unreliable generation.
core_contributions: Introduces RoseRAG: a robust RAG framework tailored for small-scale LLMs (SLMs) using margin-aware preference optimization.
Proposes contrastive preference selection that maximizes the likelihood gap between preferred and non-preferred outputs to mitigate retrieval noise.
Designs multi-turn prompting with ground-truth anchoring and rejection sampling to generate high-quality, reliable rationales for SLMs.
limitations_or_scope: Focused on open-domain QA with SLMs; assumes retriever provides candidate documents; theoretical analysis limited to idealized conditions.

problem_statement: Traditional RAG methods use static knowledge bases and fail to exploit evolving historical context in multi-turn dialogues, leading to degraded relevance and coherence.
core_contributions: Introduces DH-RAG, a novel RAG method that dynamically incorporates historical dialogue context into retrieval and generation.
Proposes a History-Learning based Query Reconstruction Module with three strategies: Historical Query Clustering, Hierarchical Matching, and Chain of Thought Tracking.
Designs a Dynamic History Information Updating Module and associated Dynamic Historical Information database for real-time context evolution.
limitations_or_scope: Focused on multi-turn dialogue; evaluation relies on adapted or domain-specific datasets (e.g., MobileCS2, CoQA); no reported cross-lingual or low-resource adaptation.

problem_statement: LLMs struggle with multi-hop reasoning over very long contexts—even with 100k+ token windows—because scattered evidence is not reliably retrieved or integrated without external mechanisms.
core_contributions: Proposes a single-pass prompt engineering method that emulates RAG by having the LLM perform both relevance tagging and chain-of-thought integration in one forward pass.
Demonstrates improved accuracy on multi-fact long-context QA tasks (e.g., object tracking, counting, indefinite knowledge) using BABILong, outperforming naive RAG and no-retrieval baselines.
Identifies critical prompt structure effects—especially instruction/question/context ordering—as key levers for robust long-context comprehension.
limitations_or_scope: Limited to single-pass, in-context emulation; may underperform on tasks requiring truly global or iterative retrieval; effectiveness depends on prompt design fidelity and model capability.

problem_statement: Semantic-only RAG retrieves isolated, redundant chunks lacking intrinsic relationships — limiting reasoning and causing fragmented prompts.
core_contributions: Introduces KG2RAG: a novel RAG framework that leverages knowledge graphs to model fact-level relationships among text chunks.
Proposes KG-guided chunk expansion to diversify and enrich retrieved content beyond semantic similarity.
Designs KG-based context organization to structure retrieved chunks into coherent, paragraph-level inputs for LLMs.
limitations_or_scope: Focused on structured KG construction from Wikipedia-style documents; relies on LLM-based triplet extraction (e.g., Llama-3); evaluation limited to HotpotQA variants.

problem_statement: Conventional RAG fails to capture complex inter-knowledge relationships; GraphRAG suffers from graph noise and incompleteness.
core_contributions: Introduces GFM-RAG, the first graph foundation model for RAG that generalizes to unseen datasets without fine-tuning
Proposes a novel graph neural network architecture that explicitly reasons over graph structure to model query-knowledge relationships
Trains an 8M-parameter GFM on large-scale heterogeneous data (60 KGs, 14M triples, 700k documents), enabling strong zero-shot retrieval
limitations_or_scope: Focuses on graph-structured knowledge integration in RAG; does not address multimodal or temporal graph extensions.

problem_statement: Despite RAG’s success in reducing hallucinations and enabling up-to-date knowledge, it introduces new risks—robustness issues, privacy leakage, adversarial attacks, and accountability gaps—that threaten its trustworthiness in high-stakes applications.
core_contributions: Proposes a unified six-dimensional framework (reliability, privacy, safety, fairness, explainability, accountability) for analyzing trustworthiness in RAG systems
Introduces structured taxonomies and evaluation protocols for each trustworthiness dimension, enabling systematic comparison of existing methods
Identifies cross-cutting research gaps and future directions—including synergies across dimensions—and curates a public GitHub resource for the community
limitations_or_scope: Focuses on conceptual organization and taxonomy; does not propose or evaluate novel algorithms or datasets.
